name: Chaker Khazaal
title: Writer, public speaker and social media specialist
bio_short: Award-winning author, public speaker and social media specialist. Ranked first in Arabian Business's 100 Most Powerful Arabs Under 40. Has spoken at the UN, Google and Meta. Executive Chairman of OBCIDO Inc. Trains in English and Arabic.
bio: Chaker is an award-winning Palestinian-Canadian author, reporter and public speaker. He has spoken at the United Nations, Google, Meta, national parliaments and major international conferences. He is the Executive Chairman of OBCIDO Inc., a New York-based digital and media company, and has published six novels, two of which appeared on Amazon's bestseller lists.  Chaker was named Esquire Middle East Man of the Year in 2015, and in 2016 was ranked first by Arabian Business in their 100 Most Powerful Arabs Under 40. In the same year, he received the Mentor Arabia Award from Queen Silvia of Sweden and Prince Turki Bin Talal Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud. In 2017, he was recognised as a Global Trailblazer alongside Arianna Huffington by Bridges of Understanding. He has been listed in Inc. Magazine's 51 Powerful Middle-Eastern Businessmen.  At ISOC, Chaker delivers training in public speaking, social media strategy, personal branding, digital communications and storytelling. His experience as a writer, speaker and media figure gives him a practitioner's perspective on how individuals and organisations can build compelling public narratives and use social media effectively. His personal journey gives his communication teaching an authenticity and conviction that resonates across cultures. Chaker is based between Paris and Dubai and trains in English and Arabic.

Magazine's 51 Powerful Middle-Eastern Businessmen and ITP Publishing's next generation of regional leaders. His journalism has focused on Palestinian and refugee issues, and he is widely recognised as an advocate for refugee communities and aspiring writers. Chaker holds a BA in international development studies from York University in Toronto. He is based between Paris and Dubai and trains in English and Arabic.
